bounds: Founder updates can help investors follow progress, but an update is not a guarantee and may not be audited or complete.
Look for a consistent time period and metrics that connect to the business plan: paying customers, revenue, retention, product milestones, cash, and hiring.
Compare the update with earlier disclosures and note what changed.
Ask whether numbers are actual results, forecasts, or goals.
In Reg CF, issuers generally have annual reporting obligations, with exceptions and specific rules; an informal monthly email is not a substitute for required filings.
For example, a fictional company might report 250 customers last quarter and 325 this quarter.
That is an increase of 75, or 30%, but it does not show revenue per customer, churn, profitability, or whether customers paid.
Watch for clear explanations of setbacks and revised plans, not only celebratory highlights.
Keep copies of updates and filings so you can compare progress over time.
